page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance from the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, translating to a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes 3780 GB of local disk capacity and is Premium Storage capable. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64lds_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 67,973.49 and a PassMark CPU score of 83,685.33. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,233.29. Memory subsystem performance is robust, showing a read-only large block bandwidth of 311.23 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 126.27 GB/sec. The instance excels in compression tasks, achieving a top-tier single-threaded gzip compression speed of 35.76 GB/sec. It also exhibits strong database capabilities, processing 109.21 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 31,743.02 on PassMark database operations.

The primary tradeoff of the D64lds_v7 is its low memory density relative to its high compute capacity, making it less suitable for memory-intensive applications. However, this resource allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, as users avoid paying for unused RAM. The inclusion of 3780 GB of local storage adds significant value for data-intensive operations. This hardware profile is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and moderate-scale LLM inference prompt processing, where its AMX instructions can be leveraged.
